The Ruperts

Normandy · Dawn · Visibility good
Objective
Notes
Opposition
Doctrine
Press Q or CRAWL to go prone. Down in the grass you are silent and all but invisible — only a sentry looking straight at you from a few metres will make you out — but weapons are slung: no rifles, no grenades until you are back on your feet, and standing up costs you half a second. Crawl into position, stand, and kill — and for the first two seconds after you come up out of a crawl, your grunts fire faster and shoot straighter than anything facing them. That window is the whole reward for the approach. Or use the knife: pick 🗡️ (or K) and tap a sentry. The nearest man goes after him alone — crawling if you are down — while the rest hold, then rises for the last few metres and does it with the stiletto. Nobody hears a thing. Send him in from behind: if the sentry turns and sees him coming, it is rifles after all. Tap the ground to call him back. Sentries hear rifles and shout to each other, so take the outliers first. Stripes are not decoration: a lance-corporal takes a fourth round, a sergeant a fifth, and every rank shoots a little straighter.
